objective.statement: Understand keys and read and write the key signatures of C, G, D and F major.
successCriteria: I know a key is the home note and scale a piece is built on.
I know a key signature puts the sharps or flats at the start of each stave.
I can name and write the key signatures of C, G, D and F major.

explanation.text: A piece in G major is built from the notes of the G major scale, and G is its home note, the tonic. We say the piece is in the key of G major.
Instead of writing F♯ every time, we put a key signature at the start of every line. It lists the sharps or flats the key needs, and they apply to every octave through the piece.

music.textAlternative: A treble stave with the key signature of G major: one sharp, F sharp, on the top line.
A bass stave with the key signature of D major: F sharp and C sharp.

explanation.caption: D major: two sharps (F♯ and C♯). The bass clef places them on different lines.

music.textAlternative: A treble stave with the key signature of F major: one flat, B flat, on the middle line.

explanation.caption: F major: one flat (B♭). C major has no key signature.

explanation.text: Sharps are added in the order F, C, G, D, A, E, B. Flats go B, E, A, D, G, C, F. Each key takes the first one or two.

music.textAlternative: The scale of G major written with its key signature of one sharp, so the F needs no sharp sign in front of it.

steps: Look at the one sharp at the start of the stave, on the top line (F).
Tap the notes from G upwards. Every F is automatically F sharp.
The scale needs no extra sharps in front of the notes because the key signature does the job.
demonstration.textAlternative: The G major scale written with a one-sharp key signature at the start of the stave.

guided.prompt: Name the major key with this key signature.
hints: F♯ sits on the top line in treble and the fourth line in bass.
For sharps, the key is a semitone above the last sharp. For flats, it is the second-to-last flat (F major has one flat).

mistakes.wrong-count: Count again: each key has a fixed number of sharps or flats.
mistakes.wrong-order: Key signatures always follow the same order. Check which comes first.
mistakes.wrong-placement: The accidentals are right, but some are on the wrong line or space for this clef.
mistakes.relative-confusion: That key shares this key signature, but it's the relative key. Check the tonic.
mistakes.mixed-sharps-flats: A key signature uses only sharps or only flats.

feedback.fallback: Not quite. Recall the order of sharps or flats and count how many the key needs.

Key signatures are written on set lines and spaces in each clef.
